title: Weighted fair queueing + tiered graceful degradation with per-customer fairness
creator: Leah Chen
description: Introduce a weighted fair queueing (WFQ) admission layer and tiered graceful degradation modes to improve fairness across customers under overload, enable region-aware preemption for multi-region failover, and provide deterministic SLO degradation profiles. This ticket designs and implements a WFQ scheduler that respects per-customer weight and SLA tier, integrates soft admission-control signals (X-Client-Score headers), and exposes runtime knobs for degradation tiers (full, reduced-ops, best-effort). Goals: reduce observed tail-latency SLO violations for high-priority tenants while preventing starvation of smaller customers; make degradation behavior predictable for product teams; allow regional controllers to apply preemption policies during cross-region failover.
acceptance_criteria: WFQ implementation accepts per-request attributes: tenant_id, weight, sla_tier, region_hint and enqueues accordingly

Under sustained overload (>=120% of capacity for 3m), high-tier requests maintain 95th p99 latency increase < 2x baseline while low-tier requests receive explicit degradation responses (503/partial) per configured quotas
System exposes API/config: per-tenant weight, global degradation profile, region-preemption enable flag
Observability: dashboards showing queue depth by tier/region, per-tenant shed rate, fairness index (Jain's index) and SLO windows updated in Console
Automated integration tests that simulate multi-region failover and validate preemption ordering and no deadlocks
Rollout completed to staging and then canary in us-west-2 with rollback path and feature flag gating
design_notes: Use a two-level queue: WFQ at front with token-bucket policing per-tenant; within each weight class, use FIFO plus a small reserve to allow short bursts
Weights derived from tenant SLA and recent usage; default weight = 1 for free tier, 4 for standard, 8 for enterprise (configurable)

Graceful degradation tiers: 0=normal, 1=content-optimized (disable expensive codecs/beam search), 2=lite-mode (reduce max tokens and model size), 3=best-effort (embedding-only or 503), with explicit response headers indicating active tier

Region-aware preemption: during cross-region failover, mark region_origin and allow preemption of lower-weight queues in the failing region to free capacity in the target region. Preemption uses soft-notify (X-Preempt-Window) so clients can retry instead of immediate kill
Admission signals: accept X-Client-Score optional header from edge layer to provide short-term priority hints (float 0..1); combine with weight to compute effective share
Avoid strict head-of-line blocking by slicing long-running generation tasks into scheduling quanta using runtime preemption points (KV-cache flush boundaries)
APIs: runtime route /config/wfq and /config/degrade to set weights and thresholds; only available to ops with RBAC
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype WFQ scheduler in the serving runtime (non-blocking) with in-memory token buckets and metrics hooks
2) Add tenant metadata propagation from API gateway to runtime (tenant_id, sla_tier, region_hint)
3) Implement degradation executor: translation of tier -> model/config overrides (batch size, quantization flag, model variant)
4) Integrate region-preemption controls and soft-notify headers in routing policy
5) Add Console panels and Alerts: queue_length_by_tier, shed_rate, fairness_index, p95/p99 latency deltas
6) Create integration tests that simulate 3-region traffic and multi-tenant overload scenarios
7) Canary rollout behind feature-flag with progressive weight enforcement and an automatic rollback script
8) Post-rollout: 2-week observation window and tune default weights
rollout_plan: Stage: unit/integration tests run in CI for all changes
Canary 1: enable WFQ in staging against synthetic load generator (100 tenants) for 48h
Canary 2: enable WFQ in us-west-2 with feature flag for 10% traffic for 72h, monitor fairness and SLOs
Global: ramp to 50% and then 100% over a week with ops on-call monitoring
Fallback: toggle feature flag off and drain queues gracefully; config rollback applies within 5 minutes
monitoring_metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency by tier and region
test_plan: Unit tests for token bucket math and WFQ share computation
Integration tests: multi-tenant burst patterns with evens/long-tail distributions; validate no starvation and weight proportional throughput
Chaos scenario: kill a region control-plane and verify preemption and cross-region failover behavior
Load test: synthetic traffic to 150% capacity for 10m and validate degradation tiers applied as configured
Regression test: ensure KV-cache preemption points do not corrupt state and generated continuity is preserved across preempt/resume
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect weight tuning causes unexpected customer outages -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-tenant dry-run mode and warning-only timeline before enforcement
Risk: head-of-line blocking with long requests -> Mitigation: enforce preemption points and max-scheduling-quanta per request
Risk: complexity of region-preemption causes split-brain decisions -> Mitigation: implement leader-elected regional controller with time-bounded leases and deterministic preemption ordering
Risk: telemetry gaps obscure fairness issues -> Mitigation: add explicit metrics and temporary high-cardinality traces for first two weeks
